findings.title: Config-driven gate has no path to configuration, and adding one contradicts the "no per-surface work" and "no 160 interfaces change" claims
findings.description: Every gate input (`workflow.review_enabled`, `review_threshold`, `review_unknown_as`, `review_gates`) lives in `ConfigManager`, but neither host class can reach it. `WorkflowNavigator` is constructed as `new WorkflowNavigator()` in `packages/cli/src/commands/next.ts:26`, `packages/cli/src/commands/status.ts:119`, and twice in `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/workflowTools.ts`; `getNext()/getStatus()/deriveSliceStatus()` accept only `ProjectData`. `ConsistencyChecker` is constructed as `new ConsistencyChecker(introspector)` in `packages/cli/src/commands/check.ts:134` and `workflowTools.ts`, with only an `IArtifactIntrospector`. Today `ConfigManager` is instantiated only in the command/tool layer (`check.ts:140`, `workflowTools.ts` `workflow_check`) to read `workflow.auto_fix`, inside a `try/catch` that silently defaults to check-only. So "the gate lives in the shared `WorkflowNavigator` and `ConsistencyChecker` ... both surfaces inherit it without per-surface work" cannot hold: either constructors change (four call sites plus `ConsistencyChecker`'s signature — a 160 interface change, contradicting Related Work's "no 160 interfaces change"), or core classes construct their own `ConfigManager`, which requires specifying the projectPath/worktree root, config error policy, and test doubles. This is the load-bearing dependency decision of the whole design and it is absent.

findings.title: Default-enabled configuration can never locate a review, and only one of the four declared transitions is representable by the proposed mechanism
findings.description: The three global keys (`:73-75`) contain no `reviewType`. Discovery at `:131` requires "the current slice index and configured reviewType" to match `NNN-review.{reviewType}.*.md`. `[workflow.review_gates]` is labeled "Optional" and `:88` says only that `workflow.review_threshold` applies "when no per-transition override exists" — it never supplies a default `reviewType`. Therefore `review_enabled = true` with the documented defaults yields zero detectable review artifacts, a permanent `pending-review`, and no way to advance. Worse, the "current transition" is never defined: `getNext()` chooses a priority branch from `SliceStatus.status`, but the status is computed earlier in `deriveSliceStatus()`, so transition selection and gate evaluation are circular. `pending-review` is defined at `:106` as "tasks complete", and the single new branch is inserted between Priority 5 and Priority 6 (`:115`) — that covers only `pre-advance`. `pre-tasks` and `pre-implementation` (`:83-84`) fire in states where tasks are not complete, and `pre-slice-plan` fires when `deriveSliceStatus()` returns `no-active-slice`; none can be expressed as two new `SliceStatus` values attached to task completion. Yet `:141` asserts "V1 implements only the four slice-level transitions" while the config table lists three slice-level transitions plus one explicitly labeled initiative-level. Since `pre-slice-plan` is deferred, v1 in fact implements one transition, not four.

findings.title: Adding a `review` slot requires interface changes the document says won't happen, and one slot cannot hold four review types
findings.description: `detectDocuments(projectPath, sliceIndex)` in `packages/core/src/introspection/parsers/documentDetector.ts` has no `reviewType` parameter, and `IArtifactIntrospector.detectDocuments` (`packages/core/src/introspection/interfaces.ts`) exposes the same signature. To filter by `reviewType`, either the signature changes (breaking `ArtifactIntrospector`, `WorkflowNavigator`, `ConsistencyChecker`, and every mock in `packages/core/tests/introspection/ConsistencyChecker.test.ts:93-95`, which builds `DocumentDetectionResult` object literals) or the detector must read config itself — which makes a stateless parser depend on the config layer and turns "no 160 interfaces change" false. A single `review` slot modeled on `sliceDesign: string | null` also cannot represent the four configured review types (`arch`, `slice`, `tasks`, `code`) for one index; `taskFile` is `string[] | null` precisely because multiple artifacts exist. Additionally `ConsistencyChecker.safeDetectDocuments()` destructures only `taskFile` and `sliceDesign`, so the new slot will not reach the checker's rules without further plumbing that is never described.

findings.title: The `validate` hook is not the fail-fast enforcement point for config the document tells users to hand-edit
findings.description: `ConfigManager.validateValue()` is invoked only from `ConfigManager.set()` (`packages/core/src/config/ConfigManager.ts:60-67`). `get()` resolves the raw TOML value via `resolveKey()` and blindly casts `projectValue as string | boolean | number`, with no `typeof` check, no `enum` check, and no `validate` call; `list()` calls `get()` the same way. The document explicitly shows the per-gate overrides (`:79-85`, `.context-forge.toml`) and `workflow.review_threshold` (`:74`) as TOML authored directly, bypassing `config_set`. An invalid `review_threshold` or an unknown gate name in a hand-edited file therefore arrives in the gate as an unrecognized string with no error — the exact "silent pass or silent block" that `:48` forbids, and a violation of the project's "Never use silent fallback values" rule. The design needs read-path validation (or a startup validation step), not just a `validate` hook on writes.

findings.title: The nested `review_gates` schema is the load-bearing decision and is deferred
findings.description: `:145` says "A decision is needed at slice design time" between extending `ConfigKeyDefinition` for nested shapes or flattening to dotted keys, but `:157` (first Anticipated Slice) already commits to "add the three global config keys and per-gate override structure to `ConfigKeys.ts`". Neither option works with the current stack: `ConfigKeyDefinition.type` is only `'string' | 'boolean' | 'number'`, `validateValue()` throws on any object (`typeof value !== def.type`), `CONFIG_KEYS` is a flat `Record<string, ConfigKeyDefinition>`, and `get()` throws `Unknown config key` for unregistered leaves. `[workflow.review_gates] pre-advance = { reviewType = ..., threshold = ... }` parses to an inline table (object), which no existing config path can validate or return. Also undefined: allowed values for `review_threshold`, `review_unknown_as`, `reviewType`, and transition names; `:48` promises "unrecognized per-gate config" fails fast but no vocabulary is given. Per CLAUDE.md ("Never scatter comparison values across code"), these need one centralized enum, not magic strings in TOML plus prose.

findings.title: Existing frontmatter machinery cannot report parse failures or represent the Squadron contract
findings.description: `packages/core/src/introspection/parsers/frontmatterParser.ts` is a flat `key: value` line splitter, not a YAML parser, and is documented "Never throws — returns `{ found: false, data: {} }` on any error". `readFile` failures (EACCES/ENOENT), missing closing `---`, and "no frontmatter" all produce the identical empty result, so `:149`'s requirement that "The rationale returned to the caller names the parse failure explicitly" is unimplementable with the named machinery; `documentDetector.safeReaddir()` likewise returns `[]` on any error, making an unreadable `reviews/` directory look like "no review artifact". `FrontmatterData` is `Record<string, string>` (`packages/core/src/introspection/types.ts`), so Squadron's `score` (float), `criteria` (dict), and `provenance` (`str | None`) degrade to strings such as `"None"` or inline dict text — `:100`'s "read and stored" and the "forward-compatible" numeric enforcement at `:169` need a typed parser that does not exist. Case/quote normalization for `verdict` is also unspecified: `verdict: pass` or `verdict: "PASS"` would be "unrecognized" and blocked by default, against the project's lenient-parsing convention. There is no `project-documents/user/reviews/` directory or review fixture in this repo, so the mandated "test fixture must include the actual format" cannot be satisfied.

findings.title: CF's own `review` frontmatter schema will validate and auto-fix the Squadron-owned artifacts the gate says it must not reinterpret
findings.description: `packages/core/src/schema/frontmatterSchema.ts` defines `FRONTMATTER_SCHEMAS.review` requiring `docType`, `project`, `status`, `dateCreated`, `dateUpdated` — and no `verdict`. `ConsistencyChecker.DOC_SCAN_DIRS` includes `reviews`, and `ruleFrontmatterSchema()` runs in `checkAll()`, which is the default for both `cf check` and `workflow_check`. That rule emits `fixable: true` `update-frontmatter` findings (e.g. `status: not_started`), so `workflow.auto_fix = true` or `cf check --fix` will write CF status fields into Squadron-produced review documents. This directly contradicts `:46` ("CF must not extend or reinterpret this schema unilaterally") and `:137` ("Neither case is auto-fixable"). CF's `status` vocabulary (`not_started/in_progress/complete/...`) is also orthogonal to Squadron's `verdict` (`PASS/CONCERNS/FAIL/UNKNOWN`); the architecture never reconciles the two contracts, even though the same `cf check` invocation will run both the old schema rule and the new review rule.

findings.title: Worktree-scoped config resolution attributed to 180 does not exist
findings.description: `ConfigManager` implements exactly two scopes (`'project' | 'user'`): `getProjectConfigPath()` is `{projectPath}/.context-forge.toml` and `getUserConfigPath()` is `{storagePath}/config.toml`. `WorktreeContext` (`packages/core/src/types/worktree.ts`) has no config fields, and `applyWorktreeOverlay()` overlays only workflow fields plus `projectPath`. 180's own architecture (`180-arch.initiative-context-worktree.md:38`) explicitly keeps "configuration" at the project layer. So "resolvable at worktree scope ... using the resolution chain 180 introduced" is either false or requires new infrastructure that the four Anticipated Slices never include. There is also an existing root mismatch: `check.ts:140` and MCP `workflow_check` construct `ConfigManager(project.projectPath)` from the base project while findings are computed over worktree-overlaid views whose `projectPath` is `wt.worktreePath`; with `review_*` keys the config root and artifact root would disagree.

findings.title: Two incompatible `recommendation` vocabularies, and the "first-class status" is not exposed on the interface runners consume
findings.description: `:20` and `:42` say the gate "returns a `pending-review` or `review-failed` recommendation"; `:118` and `:124` use `{ recommendation: "review" }` / `{ recommendation: "blocked" }`; `:173` says Amoeba consumes `review` and `blocked` and "Depend on CF returning structured `recommendation` values with a stable vocabulary — the gate must not change the `NextAction` return type". Those are three different contracts for one field. `NextAction` (`packages/core/src/introspection/types.ts:280-290`) is `{ recommendation: string, rationale, suggestedCommand?, slice?, phase?, summary, warnings? }` — no status field — so `:32`'s claim that "the visualizer and runners can act on them without parsing recommendation strings" is false for `workflow_next`; runners must substring-match English. There is no stable vocabulary to preserve: the existing advance recommendation is the free-text template `` `Advance to slice ${nextEntry.index}: ${nextEntry.name}` `` (`WorkflowNavigator.ts:253`), and `:153` discusses `workflow.auto_advance` as if a consumer exists, though `auto_advance` appears only in `ConfigKeys.ts:26` and one `ConfigManager` test. Conversely `workflow.auto_fix` *is* consumed (`check.ts:140`) and is the key that actually interacts with the new review rule, but the architecture ignores it. Also `workflow_status`'s MCP tool description enumerates the four old statuses and `workflow_next`'s description lists the response shape — both need editing, so ":34 ... without per-surface work" is inaccurate.

findings.title: Verdict matrix is undefined at its edges and `review_unknown_as` permits silent passes on corrupt reviews
findings.description: `:95` says `CONCERNS` clears at `review_threshold = "concerns"` "or lower", but no threshold vocabulary or ordering is defined (only `"pass"` and `"concerns"` appear anywhere) and `:96` says `FAIL` "always blocks", so no lower threshold can exist. `:97` defers `UNKNOWN` to `review_unknown_as` whose allowed values are never enumerated (`"fail"`, `"concern"` at `:147`, and an implied `"pending"` at `:106` — "when `review_unknown_as` treats it as pending" — with no definition). `:147` explicitly intends `review_unknown_as = "concern"` to let `UNKNOWN` clear the default `concerns` threshold; combined with `:98` (absent verdict, unrecognized value, file-read failure → `UNKNOWN`), that means malformed or unreadable review files can silently pass the gate — contradicting `:149` ("must not silently pass"), `:36` ("Conservative by default"), and the project's fail-explicitly rule. Status mapping is also missing: `pending-review` at `:106` requires "no review artifact present" and `review-failed` at `:107` requires "artifact present, verdict does not clear the threshold", so a present-but-unparseable file with `unknown_as = fail` fits neither value.

findings.title: Gate evaluation is duplicated in two components, and fail-fast config errors are swallowed by existing try/catch scaffolding
findings.description: `:22` puts "the gate logic in `WorkflowNavigator`" and ":137 a new consistency rule in `ConsistencyChecker`", and `:159-161` schedules them in separate slices. Both need config lookup, artifact discovery, frontmatter parsing, and verdict/threshold comparison, but the architecture names no shared evaluator — so the decision matrix gets implemented twice (a DRY violation) and can diverge, especially since `checkAll()` iterates every slice in every discovered slice plan while `getNext()` evaluates only the active slice. No rule states which `reviewType` applies to historical slices in `checkAll`, nor any grandfathering, so enabling gating retroactively flags every completed slice (including 900-band maintenance entries) as missing a `code` review, duplicated across worktree views before `mergeCheckResults` dedup. Meanwhile `:48` demands config errors be "surfaced immediately", but `deriveSliceStatus()` wraps its entire body in `try { ... } catch { return base; }` (`WorkflowNavigator.ts:479-496`) and `parseSlicePlanSafe`, `parseTaskFileSafe`, `safeDetectDocuments`, and `safeParseFrontmatter` all swallow exceptions: a thrown config error becomes `no-active-slice` and first-run guidance, not an error. The design needs one shared `ReviewGate` component plus an explicit error-propagation policy.

findings.title: Deferred initiative-level gate and numeric score gating cannot compose with the stated mechanism
findings.description: `:163` claims the later `pre-slice-plan` slice uses "Same gate mechanism; different insertion point in the cascade", but the mechanism is `deriveSliceStatus()`, which returns early with `no-active-slice` when `!project.fileSlice` — before `detectDocuments()` — and `getNext()`'s Priority 2 path frequently returns from `detectFirstRunContext()` before reaching any gate branch. Gating slice-plan creation therefore needs a separate state source, not a different insertion point. `NNN-review.arch.*.md` at `:141` uses an initiative index (e.g. 240), while `detectDocuments(projectPath, sliceIndex)` resolves slice/task docs by that same index; no initiative-index → review-file mapping is defined. Numeric gating is equally unsupported: `:100` says `score` is "read and stored when present" but nothing identifies the storage — `WorkflowNavigator` is stateless, `SliceStatus` has no score field, `NextAction` has none, and `DocumentDetectionResult` has no parsed-frontmatter slot. `:46`'s "It carries `criteria` and `provenance` as opaque fields ... preserved for downstream tools" is vacuous: CF never writes review artifacts, so it preserves nothing. These are extension points that will require rearchitecting, not activating a switch.

findings.title: Discovery rule cites a naming convention that is not in use here, and the tie-break can select a stale failing review
findings.description: There is no `project-documents/user/reviews/` directory in this repository and the example `210-review.code.github-copilot-vs-code-ide-support.md` does not exist, so "the existing naming convention ... no new convention is introduced" is unverifiable. What does exist conflicts: `.claude/agents/code-review-agent.md` writes `project-documents/user/reviews/review-docs/review.component.tsx.0101.md` (nested subdirectories, no `NNN-` prefix, no `reviewType` segment, YAML headers with no `verdict`) and `project-documents/user/archive/750-feature.auto-index-resolution.md:58` names `code-reviews/`. `ConsistencyChecker.DOC_SCAN_DIRS` includes `reviews` but `discoverAllDocuments()` uses non-recursive `readdir`, so the nested convention is not even scanned. No producer is named that emits `NNN-review.{reviewType}.*.md`, which leaves the "test fixture must include the actual format" rule unsatisfiable. `:133`'s "lexicographically last filename (most recent by sort order)" is also wrong for the doc's own example: filenames carry no timestamp, so the winner is the alphabetically last name slug; a stale `FAIL` review can outrank a newer `PASS` review and permanently block a pipeline unless a suffixed `-\d+` scheme (merely tolerated by `FILENAME_PARTS_RE`) is mandated. Encoding `reviewType` in a human-chosen filename slug is also the "user-accessible labels as logical structure" pattern the project conventions forbid.

findings.title: Architecture is disproportionate to the one behavioral change required; concrete cut list
findings.description: `riskLevel: low` and a single deliverable ("stop recommending advance when a review is missing or failing") have grown into 3 global keys, a nested 4-transition override table, 2 new statuses, 2 new recommendation tokens, an `review_unknown_as` × `review_threshold` cross-product, score/criteria/provenance handling with "no v1 consumer", a "forward-compatible" numeric-enforcement code path, a multi-file tie-break rule, and 4 slices — one of which (`:157`) is a pure refactor ("Includes renumbering the `getNext()` priority cascade. No gate logic yet") and another (`:163`) is explicitly deferred. Cut from v1: the entire `[workflow.review_gates]` table plus `pre-tasks`, `pre-implementation`, and `pre-slice-plan` (ship only `pre-advance` with a single `code` reviewType); `review_unknown_as` (treat anything not `PASS`/`CONCERNS` as blocking); "read and stored" score and the opaque `criteria`/`provenance` carrying; the standalone priority-renumbering slice; and the initiative-level slice. Drop the worktree-scope requirement at `:171` until the config infrastructure exists. Deferring is not free: the initiative plan (`project-documents/user/project-guides/001-initiative-plan.context-forge.md:31`) assigns "which states require a review artifact (`workflow.review_required`)" to this initiative, and the architecture replaces it with `review_enabled` + per-gate overrides while deferring all but one actual state. Also note `:151` justifies renumbering "to avoid fractional priorities" even though `WorkflowNavigator.ts:186` already contains a `Priority 2.5` branch — the refactor solves a problem the code does not have.
